Sky: cooking without management · expanded view

Sky likes planning the order of cooking tasks, testing a recipe and preparing food safely for others. Owning a restaurant, bargaining and supervising staff are not appealing. Many official activities are unrelated to cooking and receive unsure or dislike responses; the detailed food interest should still be visible as something to explore, not a forced management identity.

Narrative model, with its answers frozen before the first run. Optional questions omitted by the shorter route are marked. These are synthetic checks, not observations of students.

Authored model & first-run review

Prepares several family meals each week and helped at a supervised school food event. Adult oversight is still needed for large-service food safety.

Cooking at home is neither a professional aptitude result nor proof that restaurant work, hours or earnings will suit Sky.

Choice screens: 97 including lifestyle and profession questions; introductory screens are not counted.

Low experience does not change interests or career rankings · A more expensive lifestyle changes money needs, not interest matching · Answers and recommendations survive save/reload · Open profiles do not force three pathways or a profession · Optional detail preserves all six official interest scores · Plan creation preserves earlier completed work, notes and official answers
